reasons.plausibility: The hypothesis incorrectly assumes that severe plastic deformation and grain refinement will improve oxidation and liquid-metal corrosion resistance, whereas well-established science shows that high grain-boundary density typically accelerates these degradation processes in ultra-high-temperature ceramics.
reasons.testability: The proposed test is clear and comparative, but the falsification criteria are tied to specific, large quantitative improvements (e.g., 70% toughness increase) that are not physically justified, making the test a strawman rather than a decisive evaluation of the core mechanism.
reasons.usefulness: The hypothesis is not useful because it proposes a mechanism (grain refinement for better oxidation/corrosion resistance) that contradicts fundamental materials science for this class of materials, leading researchers down an unproductive path.
